Sometimes the most meaningful improvements start with a simple question: what would make this easier for everyone?

I recently reflected on an experience coordinating a shared project calendar and gathering feedback from colleagues. What stood out was not just the calendar itself, but the conversations around it. People brought different perspectives to the same shared work, and listening helped me see how important it is to make space for those perspectives.

A shared tool can be useful, but its real value depends on how people experience it. Taking the time to ask for feedback is a way to understand that experience and keep collaboration at the center of the process.

This experience reminded me that listening is not an extra step. It is part of building a way of working that people can understand and use together. I am grateful for the perspectives colleagues shared and for the opportunity to learn from them.

How do you make space for feedback when your team is working together?
